reference_contract.cache: Cache entries own their copied native-name key and node allocation. The mapped resource at node+14 is a raw non-retained pointer: temporary-pair construction, node construction and insertion add no reference; single erase (prior packet) and full subtree clear release no resource. Under the verified normal route the cache is a non-owning name index.
reference_contract.new_caller: Prior factory/base-construction audit establishes new resource initial reference count1; this packet proves cache insertion does not create another reference and the load miss returns manager.currentResource+24 unchanged by insertion. The caller receives the factory-provided reference; this packet does not claim every arbitrary factory follows that initial-reference contract.
reference_contract.cache_hit_dependency: The existing00b80720 load audit establishes InterlockedIncrement(resource+4) on a cache hit before returning the pointer. That caller operation creates the hit caller reference; it is separate from cache ownership. docs/VFS_LOAD_WORKER_DISPATCH.md
reference_contract.destruction_dependency: Prior00b88430 resource destructor removes one equivalent cache name through00b801c0 without mapped-value identity comparison. Combined with non-retaining insertion/non-releasing erase, reference owners outside the cache govern resource lifetime. docs/RESOURCE_CLASSIFICATION_AND_CACHE_ERASE.md
reference_contract.scratch_fields: Manager destruction does not directly release current factory+20 or current resource+24. Its manager+4 polymorphic object and secondary tree+8 cleanup are separate external ownership contracts; do not call the whole manager destructor globally non-releasing.

duplicate_and_null_contract.key: Insertion uses length0 empty markers and CRTstricmp for nonempty strings, matching previous find/erase comparator. Valid map ordering and structural helper behavior are assumed.
duplicate_and_null_contract.duplicate: Equivalent name returns existing owner/node iterator with inserted byte0. It does not replace mapped pointer, allocate a new node, increment size, retain new/existing resource, or release the rejected source resource. Source temporary key is cleaned by caller later. Different name keys are not rejected merely because raw resource pointers are equal.
duplicate_and_null_contract.load_caller_ignores_result: 00b80975 calls unique insertion, then immediately cleans temporary names; no inserted-byte/returned-node test occurs before00b809e0 loads manager.currentResource+24 and00b80a2e returns it. Thus if a duplicate is encountered after the miss path has constructed a different resource, the old cache mapping remains and the new currentResource is still returned.
duplicate_and_null_contract.combined_erase_consequence: If such a rejected new resource later reaches its last reference, its prior verified destructor erases by name only, which can remove the old equivalent-name cache entry. This is an inference combining matched insertion/caller and prior name-erase bodies; no concurrent or reentrant duplicate scenario was reproduced.
duplicate_and_null_contract.nulls: Null raw resource values can be stored without dereference by these cache insert/clear helpers. A null source-pair/name-pair address is invalid; nonempty string data must be valid. Prior cache-hit caller dereferences mappedResource+4, so a null stored value is outside the full load/hit contract.

manager_teardown.cache_path: Pass full begin/head range for tree at+14 to00b805d0. Its optimized whole-tree branch invokes00b7ff20 onhead.parent, clears tree links/count, and manager then frees head/sentinel.
manager_teardown.clear_order: Destroy right subtree recursively, destroy current key/node, then iterate left; sentinel flag+19 terminates. Left link is saved before node free. Mapped resource+14 is neither read nor released.
manager_teardown.remaining_fields: Polymorphic manager+4 is called virtual+0(flags1) before tree clear. Secondary tree+8 is cleared through00b80500 after resource cache. Those methods remain external. Then singleton010901c4 is zeroed andbase vtable00ce3818 installed.
manager_teardown.lifetime_limit: Because cache teardown does not destroy mapped resources, remaining external resource references can outlive the map. Actual singleton/resource shutdown order and behavior of their later name-removal callbacks remain outside this audit.
